note: Window agent p1400-p1499, 1 Nov 2026. Eight corrections: Inca Altiplano hole 1482-1496; Lithuania's one-year Black Sea blip in 1401; Ming vs Mongol Khanate over Gansu and Qinghai 1455-1467; English Normandy unowned 1436-1449; the Duchy of Pomerania and the Duchy of Wurttemberg absorbed by a 'merge' event whose counterpart has no dossier (1478, 1482); Guelders not restored in 1492.

region.text: with the Lauenburg and Bütow Land

events.note: 1478: the duchy is reunited, not absorbed. The Duchy of Pomerania page: 'Reunited under Bogislaw X: 1478' and 'The country existed as a united duchy between years 1121-1160, 1264-1295, 1478-1531, and 1625-1637'; 'Vassal of the Holy Roman Empire (1227-1637)'. The dossier's own 1478 'merge' event names two lines with no dossier as counterpart, so the compiler absorbed the whole duchy (108 cells to nobody) and the draft has no Pomerania from 1478 to 1499. This event gives the reunited duchy's land (the 1466 keyframe shape) back.

region.text: the county (duchy from 21 July 1495) with Montbéliard in the west, held by the House of Württemberg from 1444

events.note: 1482: Wurttemberg is reunited, not absorbed. County of Wurttemberg page: 'As a result of the Treaty of Munsingen in 1482' the realm was reunited and 'Count Eberhard V succeeded in reuniting Wurttemberg'; 'In 1495 ... the county became the Duchy of Wurttemberg.' The dossier's 1482 'merge' event names the Urach line, which has no dossier, so the compiler absorbed Wurttemberg's land (the Stuttgart area, 21 cells) and the draft shows no Wurttemberg round Stuttgart from 1482 to 1519. This event gives the 1444 keyframe shape back.

1492: Charles of Egmond is restored. Duchy of Guelders page: 'In 1492, the citizens of Guelders ... ransomed Charles and recognized him as their Duke'; the duchy kept its independence until the Treaty of Venlo (1543). The dossier's 1492 occupation_end has nothing to hand back: the cells were Burgundian (direct) to 1481, nobody in 1482-1491 and are given to the empire's catch-all by the Habsburg shape change of 1492, so the draft has no Guelders from 1473 to the end of the window.

region.text: the Duchy of Guelders: the cells Maximilian's Habsburg monarchy still holds in 1491 (the Upper Quarter round Roermond and the western Veluwe)

events.note: 1492: the rest of Guelders returns to Charles of Egmond. Duchy of Guelders page: after Charles the Bold's death 'Guelders was ruled by Habsburg Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I', and 'In 1492, the citizens of Guelders, who had become disenchanted with the rule of Maximilian' ransomed Charles and recognized him as their Duke. events/2 of this file (counterpart the Empire's catch-all, which holds none of the region in 1491) takes only the 22 unowned cells; the 9 cells habsburg-monarchy holds in 1491 (Roermond, the western Veluwe, near Tiel and Sittard) pass to the Empire's catch-all and Habsburg in 1492. A gain takes only one counterpart's cells, hence this second event. [Added by the reviewer of p1400-p1499, 1 Nov 2026.]

union.text: the Altiplano of the Aymara kingdoms, Inca land since 1477 and drawn by Cliopatria from its 1497 shape

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1482 shape plus the Altiplano the Aymara kingdoms lost to the Inca in 1477, kept through 1496 until the 1497 shape

keyframe_overrides.why: The Aymara page: the Pacajes (La Paz), Lupacas and Collas (Puno) 'accepted the dominion of Cusco' and the kingdoms (c. 1151-1477) 'disappeared due to the military conquest of the Inca Empire'; nothing returns them to independence. Cliopatria's 1482 outline omits them, so the draft drops the 1477 gain (1,385 Bolivian cells) to nobody for 1482-1496 until the 1497 shape restores it. The Altiplano stays Inca from 1477.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1402 shape: the Lithuanian realm without Smolensk (revolted 1401), without Samogitia (ceded 1398) and without the Black Sea coast and southern steppe (lost at the Vorskla, 12 August 1399)

keyframe_overrides.why: The Vorskla page: 'Lithuania loses the Black Sea coast and southern part of the Wild Fields to the Tatars' (12 August 1399), and the dossier's own 1399 loss gives them to the Golden Horde. The one-year 1401 keyframe is Cliopatria's 1395 shape, which still has that coast, so the draft hands 353 steppe cells back to Lithuania for 1401 only and the size rule then decides a 705 cell-year conflict with the Golden Horde.

region.text: Qinghai and Gansu, the Ming's north-western provinces in Cliopatria's Ming shape to 1467

rulings.why: The Hexi Corridor page: 'In 1370, the newly-established Ming dynasty seized the eastern section of the Hexi Corridor from the Mongols' and 'captured most of the remaining territory in 1372', with garrison towns along the frontier; 'In 1524, Jiayu Pass was closed'. Neither this page nor the Qinghai page gives the Mongol Khanate of 1455 any of this land (the Hexi page leaves Dunhuang beyond Jiayu Pass 'under the control of the Northern Yuan dynasty' in 1372, and the Qinghai page has most of Qinghai under the early Ming only 'for a short time', 'later gradually lost to the Khoshut Khanate'), so the ruling keeps the Ming dossier's land to its own 1468 loss rather than asserting Ming rule there. The Mongol Khanate's 1455 keyframe stretches Cliopatria's 1468 shape back to Esen's death and the size rule gave it 2,431 Ming cells for 1455-1467; the 2,169 of them in Gansu and Qinghai stay Ming under this ruling. [Reviewer, 1 Nov 2026: why rewritten to quote the pages in full; entry unchanged.]
